Vectors and dyadics of a coordinate system

Source: R/vector-basis.R
VectorAdd.Rd

VectorAdd(), VectorMul(), DyadicAdd() and DyadicMul() build sums and scalar multiples of vectors and dyadics, as the arithmetic operators do. VectorZero() and DyadicZero() are the zero vector and the zero dyadic (Vector.zero and Dyadic.zero in SymPy). BaseVector(index, system) is a basis vector of a CoordSys3D() and BaseDyadic(v1, v2) the outer product of two basis vectors. measure_number() and base_vector() give the parts of a VectorMul; components() the components of a vector or dyadic as a named list.

Usage

VectorAdd(...)

VectorMul(...)

VectorZero()

DyadicAdd(...)

DyadicMul(...)

DyadicZero()

BaseVector(index, system)

BaseDyadic(vector1, vector2)

measure_number(v)

Arguments

...

Vectors or dyadics, and scalars.

index

An integer 0, 1 or 2.

system

A CoordSys3D().

vector1, vector2

Base vectors.

v

A vector or dyadic.

Value

A vector or dyadic.

Details

Vectors support +, -, multiplication and division by scalars, & for the dot product and | for the outer product; ^ raises an error as SymPy's ** does. Use cross() for the cross product.

Examples

C <- CoordSys3D("C")
v <- 3 * C$i + C$x * C$j
v
#> 3*C.i + C.x*C.j
VectorAdd(C$i, C$j, C$i)
#> 2*C.i + C.j
VectorMul(2, C$k)
#> 2*C.k
C$i | C$j
#> (C.i|C.j)
